operation.summary: A GraphQL query
operation.description: Reads what it names. A query cannot change anything: a mutation is its own operation, named by its field.

operation.summary: Publishes an activity to your agent’s session and updates its lifecycle.
operation.description: Publishes an activity to your agent’s session and updates its lifecycle. Thoughts and actions report ongoing work; a response completes the turn unless it has the continue signal, an elicitation waits for user input, and an error records a failed turn. The session must be unarchived and owned by the authenticated app user. Use the agent app’s OAuth or workload identity token; personal API keys cannot publish agent activities.

operation.summary: Starts an active session for your authenticated agent app on an existing issue comment thread.
operation.description: Starts an active session for your authenticated agent app on an existing issue comment thread. Supply the UUID of an unarchived root comment; replies and threads that already have a session are rejected. The caller must have access to the issue. Use the returned session ID when publishing activities.

operation.summary: Starts an active session for your authenticated agent app and creates its comment thread on the issue.
operation.description: Starts an active session for your authenticated agent app and creates its comment thread on the issue. The issue must be accessible and writable. Supply its UUID or identifier, then use the returned session ID to publish progress and results with agentActivityCreate.

operation.summary: Updates your agent’s session title, external links, or plan.
operation.description: Updates your agent’s session title, external links, or plan. Only the app user that owns the session can change these fields. Omitted fields remain unchanged, while each supplied plan or externalUrls list replaces that value. Updates other than a title-only change acknowledge a pending or stale session by making it active; publishing an activity still determines the next turn status.

operation.summary: Updates external links on a session owned by the authenticated agent app.
operation.description: Updates external links on a session owned by the authenticated agent app. A pending or stale session becomes active.

operation.summary: Creates reusable Markdown instructions for the Linear Agent, owned by the authenticated user.
operation.description: Creates reusable Markdown instructions for the Linear Agent, owned by the authenticated user. Omit teamId for a personal skill, or provide a team UUID to share it with that team. Creating a team skill requires permission to manage the team’s agent skills. The returned skill contains the saved instructions and display details.

operation.summary: Deletes an agent skill and its inherited copies.
operation.description: Deletes an agent skill and its inherited copies. Inherited skills must be deleted from the team that owns the source skill.

operation.summary: Updates a skill the caller can manage.
operation.description: Updates a skill the caller can manage. Omitted fields remain unchanged, and a supplied body replaces the full instruction text. For a team skill, the caller needs agent skill management permission; moving it also requires that permission in the destination team. Inherited copies cannot be edited directly—update their source skill instead.

operation.summary: Registers an export key for Airbyte.
operation.description: Registers an export key for Airbyte. Requires integration-creation and export permissions and a plan with data export. The key can read private-team data.

operation.summary: Creates an attachment, or updates the existing attachment with the same URL on the same issue.
operation.description: Creates an attachment, or updates the existing attachment with the same URL on the same issue. This is useful for links and metadata managed by your integration. Use attachmentLinkURL or a service-specific link mutation when you want Linear to fetch integration metadata and apply its supported link behavior.

operation.summary: Deletes the attachment record from its issue.
operation.description: Deletes the attachment record from its issue. This removes the link in Linear; it does not delete the external resource.

operation.summary: Link a Discord message to an issue.
operation.description: Link a Discord message to an issue. Requires a connected Discord integration.

operation.summary: Link a Front conversation to an issue.
operation.description: Link a Front conversation to an issue. Requires a connected Front integration.

operation.summary: Link a GitHub issue to a Linear issue.
operation.description: Link a GitHub issue to a Linear issue. Uses the matching GitHub integration and sync mapping when available; may fall back to a URL attachment.

operation.summary: Link a GitHub pull request to an issue.
operation.description: Link a GitHub pull request to an issue. Uses the matching GitHub integration when available; may fall back to a URL attachment.

operation.summary: Links a GitLab merge request to an issue.
operation.description: Links a GitLab merge request to an issue. Supply the merge-request URL, number, and full project path including any groups. Linear uses a matching integration when available and otherwise creates a basic URL attachment.

operation.summary: Link an Intercom conversation to an issue.
operation.description: Link an Intercom conversation to an issue. Requires a connected Intercom integration.

operation.summary: Links a Jira issue to a Linear issue.
operation.description: Links a Jira issue to a Linear issue. The URL selects a connected Jira site; if it identifies no connected site, Linear uses the workspace’s sole Jira integration. With multiple Jira integrations, provide a URL for the intended site.

operation.summary: Link a Salesforce case to an issue.
operation.description: Link a Salesforce case to an issue. Requires a connected Salesforce integration and a valid case URL.

operation.summary: Link an existing Slack message to an issue.
operation.description: Link an existing Slack message to an issue. This creates a rich attachment using the workspace's Slack integration.

operation.summary: Links a URL to an issue and, when recognized, uses the workspace’s matching integration to fetch richer details.
operation.description: Links a URL to an issue and, when recognized, uses the workspace’s matching integration to fetch richer details. Supported integrations can add behaviors such as status updates. If no matching integration can enrich the link, Linear creates a basic URL attachment.

operation.summary: Link a Zendesk ticket to an issue.
operation.description: Link a Zendesk ticket to an issue. Requires a connected Zendesk integration.

operation.summary: Sync an existing Slack attachment with an issue comment thread and import existing replies.
operation.description: Sync an existing Slack attachment with an issue comment thread and import existing replies. Requires a connected Slack integration whose bot can post in the channel; the Slack thread cannot already be synced elsewhere.

operation.summary: Updates an existing attachment’s title, subtitle, metadata, or icon.
operation.description: Updates an existing attachment’s title, subtitle, metadata, or icon. title is required even when changing another field, and metadata replaces the full stored object. This mutation does not move the attachment or change its URL.

operation.summary: Creates a comment on one resource, or a reply when parentId is supplied.
operation.description: Creates a comment on one resource, or a reply when parentId is supplied. You must be allowed to comment on that resource. For issue comments, the author is subscribed to the issue unless doNotSubscribeToIssue is true.

operation.summary: Deletes a comment and, for a root comment, its replies.
operation.description: Deletes a comment and, for a root comment, its replies. You must be allowed to delete the comment and comment on its resource. Deleting a reply selected as the resolution reopens the parent thread.

operation.summary: Marks a root comment’s thread as resolved by you.
operation.description: Marks a root comment’s thread as resolved by you. You may select one of its replies as resolvingCommentId, or resolve the thread without a specific reply. Pass the root comment ID, even when the discussion ended in a reply.

operation.summary: Reopens a resolved thread and clears its resolution time, resolving user, and selected resolving reply.
operation.description: Reopens a resolved thread and clears its resolution time, resolving user, and selected resolving reply. Pass the root comment ID. An already unresolved thread is returned unchanged.

operation.summary: Replaces a comment’s Markdown body and records an edit time.
operation.description: Replaces a comment’s Markdown body and records an edit time. Content edits are restricted to an authorized author or acting user; comments originating in synced Slack messages or Intercom cannot be edited here. Omit body to keep the existing message.

operation.summary: Submits a message to Linear support on behalf of the authenticated user.
operation.description: Submits a message to Linear support on behalf of the authenticated user. Delivery happens after the request succeeds.

operation.summary: Queues a workspace CSV export and emails the requesting user a download link when it is ready.
operation.description: Queues a workspace CSV export and emails the requesting user a download link when it is ready. Success confirms scheduling, not completion. Private and restricted teams are excluded unless explicitly selected by their UUIDs. Requires workspace export permission, which permits selecting eligible teams even when the requester is not a member.

operation.summary: Create a notification to remind a user about an initiative update.
Create a notification to remind a user about a project update.
Creates a saved view owned by you.
operation.description: Creates a saved view owned by you. Choose an issue, project, initiative, or update filter and set shared if others in its scope should use it. Display settings can be saved separately with viewPreferencesCreate.

operation.summary: Deletes a saved view without deleting the items it displayed.
operation.description: Deletes a saved view without deleting the items it displayed. Only workspace members can delete views shared with the whole workspace; deleting a view used in a pinned tab also requires permission to edit that tab. Use customViewHasSubscribers to check whether other people receive notifications from the view.

operation.summary: Updates a saved view’s metadata, scope, or filter configuration.
operation.description: Updates a saved view’s metadata, scope, or filter configuration. Omitted fields are unchanged. Only workspace members can change views shared with the whole workspace; editing a view used in a pinned tab also requires permission to edit that tab.

operation.summary: Creates a customer when the Customers feature is available and enabled in the workspace.
operation.description: Creates a customer when the Customers feature is available and enabled in the workspace. Business domains and external IDs must not belong to another customer, including archived customers. If no status is supplied, the first customer status by position is used.

operation.summary: Permanently deletes a customer, including an archived customer.
operation.description: Permanently deletes a customer, including an archived customer. Use customerMerge when you want to preserve its requests by transferring them to another customer.

operation.summary: Merges two customers by transferring all needs from the source customer to the target customer.
operation.description: Merges two customers by transferring all needs from the source customer to the target customer. The source customer is archived after the merge. Domains, external IDs, and metadata are combined on the target customer.

operation.summary: Archives a customer need so it can be removed from active request lists without permanently deleting it.
operation.description: Archives a customer need so it can be removed from active request lists without permanently deleting it. Use customerNeedUnarchive to restore the saved need.

operation.summary: Records customer feedback, optionally linked to an issue.
operation.description: Records customer feedback, optionally linked to an issue. Unlinked requests require Customer Signals to be enabled. You can identify the customer, add Markdown feedback, or link a source attachment. Multiple requests can be recorded for the same customer and issue.

operation.summary: Creates a customer need from an existing issue attachment.
operation.description: Creates a customer need from an existing issue attachment. If that attachment already has an archived need, the need is restored and follows the attachment’s current issue. An existing active need is not duplicated.

operation.summary: Permanently deletes a customer need.
operation.description: Permanently deletes a customer need. By default, its associated issue or project attachment is also deleted. Set keepAttachment to true to retain that source attachment; the linked issue or project is kept.

operation.summary: Restores an archived customer need.
operation.description: Restores an archived customer need. The need must currently be archived; its saved feedback and associations are kept.

operation.summary: Updates a customer request, including its feedback, customer, priority, or issue association.
operation.description: Updates a customer request, including its feedback, customer, priority, or issue association. Only manually added source attachments can be replaced or removed. Use clearAttachment to remove such a source; moving the request to another issue also moves its source attachment.

operation.summary: Creates a workspace customer status.
operation.description: Creates a workspace customer status. Requires permission to manage customer settings and rejects a name or display name already used by another active status.

operation.summary: Deletes a customer status.
operation.description: Deletes a customer status. Cannot delete the last remaining status in a workspace, and the status must not be in use by any customers.

operation.summary: Updates a workspace customer status.
operation.description: Updates a workspace customer status. Requires permission to manage customer settings. Customers using the status retain their association with it.

operation.summary: Creates a workspace customer tier.
operation.description: Creates a workspace customer tier. Requires permission to manage customer settings and rejects a name or display name already used by another active tier.

operation.summary: Deletes a customer tier.
operation.description: Deletes a customer tier. The tier must not be in use by any customers.

operation.summary: Updates a workspace customer tier.
operation.description: Updates a workspace customer tier. Requires permission to manage customer settings. Customers using the tier retain their association with it.

operation.summary: Disconnects a customer from its configured data source integration so the integration no longer updates it.
operation.description: Disconnects a customer from its configured data source integration so the integration no longer updates it. External IDs belonging to that source are cleared. Requires permission to manage workspace customer settings.

operation.summary: Updates the supplied customer fields, leaving omitted fields unchanged.
operation.description: Updates the supplied customer fields, leaving omitted fields unchanged. For a customer managed by an integration, only fields that are editable in Linear are applied; managed fields are ignored. The request fails if none of the supplied fields are editable.

operation.summary: Finds a customer using the supplied UUID, external ID, Slack channel, or domains, and updates it; otherwise creates one.
operation.description: Finds a customer using the supplied UUID, external ID, Slack channel, or domains, and updates it; otherwise creates one. A name is required when no customer matches. Unlike customerUpdate, this operation can override integration-managed fields, and a tierName can create a new customer tier when the caller has permission to manage customer settings.

operation.summary: Archives a cycle and removes its current issues from it.
operation.description: Archives a cycle and removes its current issues from it. The issues themselves are not archived. An inherited cycle must be managed through its parent team. Requires permission to manage the team.

operation.summary: Unsupported.
operation.description:
Unsupported. This mutation always returns an error; cycles are generated from the team’s cycle settings.

Deprecated: Cycle creation is not supported.

operation.summary: Shifts an upcoming cycle and every later cycle in the team by the same number of days.
operation.description: Shifts an upcoming cycle and every later cycle in the team by the same number of days. Local times are preserved in the team’s time zone, and the team’s cycle start day is updated. Use this when moving the schedule as a whole; it requires permission to manage the team.

operation.summary: Starts the upcoming cycle as of midnight today.
operation.description: Starts the upcoming cycle as of midnight today. Completes the previous cycle if it has not yet ended. Only the next upcoming (not yet started) cycle for the team can be started. Requires permission to manage the team.

operation.summary: Updates a cycle’s name, description, or schedule and returns the resulting cycle.
operation.description: Updates a cycle’s name, description, or schedule and returns the resulting cycle. Date changes can shorten adjacent cycles to prevent overlap. You cannot change an active cycle’s start or a completed cycle’s dates, or edit inherited cycles directly. Requires permission to manage the team.

operation.summary: Creates a document in a project, issue, or release, or in your private documents with personalUserId, with optional initial Markdown content.
operation.description: Creates a document in a project, issue, or release, or in your private documents with personalUserId, with optional initial Markdown content. The returned document includes its assigned UUID and metadata; select content to read the resulting body.

operation.summary: Moves a document to the trash and archives it, including the sub-documents covered by its archive cascade.
operation.description: Moves a document to the trash and archives it, including the sub-documents covered by its archive cascade. It is not permanently removed by this mutation. You must be allowed to manage the document, or to edit it when it is a page of a private document; use documentUnarchive to restore it.

operation.summary: Shares a document and its sub-documents with workspace members at a role.
operation.description: Shares a document and its sub-documents with workspace members at a role. On a personal document only the owner can share it. On any other document the owner, an owner of one of its teams, or a workspace admin can, the people must be able to see the document, and the role must be above its general access. People it is newly shared with are subscribed to the document. Users who already have another role move to the given one.

operation.summary: Restores a trashed document and its eligible sub-documents.
operation.description: Restores a trashed document and its eligible sub-documents. You must be allowed to manage the restored documents, or to edit them when they are pages of a private document. If the containing resource is archived, restore that resource first.

operation.summary: Stops sharing a document and its sub-documents with users.
operation.description: Stops sharing a document and its sub-documents with users. Whoever can manage access to the document can remove anyone it is shared with; anyone else can only remove themselves.

operation.summary: Updates a document’s metadata or replaces its Markdown body.
operation.description: Updates a document’s metadata or replaces its Markdown body. You must have edit access to the document. Supplying a different container moves the document there, which can affect access; omitted fields are left unchanged.

operation.summary: Changes what users other than the owner can do with a document that is not personal: edit, comment, or view.
operation.description: Changes what users other than the owner can do with a document that is not personal: edit, comment, or view. Only the owner of the document, an owner of one of its teams, or a workspace admin can change it. Comment and view need an owner who can access the document.

operation.summary: Changes what people outside a document's teams can do with a document in a public team or in a project with a public team: edit, comment, or view.
operation.description: Changes what people outside a document's teams can do with a document in a public team or in a project with a public team: edit, comment, or view. It can't be above the document's general access. Only the owner of the document, an owner of one of its teams, or a workspace admin can change it. Comment and view need an owner who can access the document.

operation.summary: Creates an address that accepts email for one team or issue template.
operation.description: Creates an address that accepts email for one team or issue template. For team and template types, an existing active address for that destination is returned instead of creating another. Use the returned emailAddress as the forwarding destination in your mail provider. Asks creation requires the appropriate plan and integration management permission; team and template addresses require permission to manage their destination. Form templates cannot be used for template intake.

operation.summary: Deletes an email intake address object.
Requests a check of the intake address’s custom sending domain after you update its DNS records.
operation.description: Requests a check of the intake address’s custom sending domain after you update its DNS records. The check runs asynchronously: success means a check was requested, not that the domain passed verification. Query sesDomainIdentity.canSendFromCustomDomain and dnsRecords for the result. Returns success=false when no custom domain is configured or the domain is already fully verified.

operation.summary: Generates a new email address for an existing team or template intake configuration.
operation.description: Generates a new email address for an existing team or template intake configuration. The old address no longer routes incoming mail, so update any forwarding rules or places where you published it. The intake record and its settings are retained. Asks and Asks web addresses do not support rotation through this mutation.

operation.summary: Updates an existing email intake address.
Completes email sign-in using the emailed token and the same clientAuthCode sent with emailUserAccountAuthChallenge.
operation.description: Completes email sign-in using the emailed token and the same clientAuthCode sent with emailUserAccountAuthChallenge. Successful authentication consumes the client binding and sets a session cookie. Use the returned memberships and available or locked workspaces to continue into a workspace; the deprecated token field is not populated. An expired token or a code from a different client cannot complete this flow.

operation.summary: Unsubscribes a user from the selected email category using the user ID and token from a Linear email.
operation.description: Unsubscribes a user from the selected email category using the user ID and token from a Linear email. No sign-in is required because the token authorizes the change. An invalid token returns success=false; other email categories and notification channels are unchanged.

operation.summary: Starts email sign-in and sends a one-time token to the supplied address.
operation.description: Starts email sign-in and sends a one-time token to the supplied address. Generate and retain a clientAuthCode UUID, then pass it with the emailed token to emailTokenUserAccountAuth within ten minutes. Requesting another challenge replaces the stored client binding for that email. When login challenge verification is enabled, challengeResponse is also required. Success confirms the challenge was accepted; email delivery may finish in the background.

operation.summary: Creates a custom emoji from an image already uploaded to Linear.
operation.description: Creates a custom emoji from an image already uploaded to Linear. Its name must be unique in the workspace. The current user is recorded as the creator, and the source is user.

operation.summary: Deletes an emoji.
Adds an external resource to an initiative, project, or release the caller can access and write to.
operation.description: Adds an external resource to an initiative, project, or release the caller can access and write to. Provide exactly one parent, a destination URL, and the label to show in Linear. Omit sortOrder to place the link last among the parent’s resources. This stores a reference to the URL; it does not upload or copy the destination content.

operation.summary: Removes a resource link from Linear and clears any team pins that refer to it.
operation.description: Removes a resource link from Linear and clears any team pins that refer to it. The external URL’s content is unchanged. The caller must have access to the link’s parent scope; archived links can also be deleted.

operation.summary: Changes an unarchived resource link’s URL, display label, or position within its parent’s resources.
operation.description: Changes an unarchived resource link’s URL, display label, or position within its parent’s resources. Omitted fields remain unchanged, and the parent cannot be changed. The link must be writable and within the caller’s permitted scope.

operation.summary: Creates a sidebar favorite for the authenticated user.
operation.description: Creates a sidebar favorite for the authenticated user. If it already exists, updates its position and supplied folder instead.

operation.summary: Removes a favorite from your sidebar.
operation.description: Removes a favorite from your sidebar. Deleting a custom folder also removes the favorites inside it; the bookmarked entities are unaffected. The mutation succeeds if the favorite no longer exists.

operation.summary: Changes the position, parent folder, or name of one of your favorites.
operation.description: Changes the position, parent folder, or name of one of your favorites. Omitted fields stay unchanged. The target entity cannot be changed, and predefined live folders cannot be renamed.

operation.summary: Prepares a file upload and returns a signed destination.
operation.description: Prepares a file upload and returns a signed destination. Upload the raw bytes with HTTP PUT to uploadFile.uploadUrl, using its headers and the supplied Content-Type; start the request within one minute and send exactly size bytes. Once the PUT succeeds, reference uploadFile.assetUrl in an issue description, comment, or attachment. This mutation does not create that reference for you. Workspace file-type restrictions and plan upload limits apply.

operation.summary: Permanently delete an uploaded file by asset URL.
operation.description: Permanently delete an uploaded file by asset URL. This should be used as a last resort and will break comments and documents that reference the asset.

operation.summary: Creates a rule that maps a Git event to an issue status for a team.
operation.description: Creates a rule that maps a Git event to an issue status for a team. Requires permission to manage that team. Rules cannot be created for retired teams.

operation.summary: Permanently deletes a Git automation rule.
operation.description: Permanently deletes a Git automation rule. Requires permission to manage its team. Removing a branch-specific rule allows the team’s default for that event to apply again.

operation.summary: Updates the status, branch scope, or event of an existing rule.
operation.description: Updates the status, branch scope, or event of an existing rule. Requires permission to manage its team, and the team must not be retired. Omitted fields keep their values.

operation.summary: Creates a team’s target-branch pattern for Git automation.
operation.description: Creates a team’s target-branch pattern for Git automation. Add automation rules that reference the returned definition to choose the status changes. Requires team-management permission and an active, non-retired team.

operation.summary: Deletes a target-branch definition and its associated automation rules.
operation.description: Deletes a target-branch definition and its associated automation rules. Future matching events use any remaining applicable rules, including team defaults. Requires team-management permission.

operation.summary: Changes the pattern or matching mode used by every automation rule linked to this definition.
operation.description: Changes the pattern or matching mode used by every automation rule linked to this definition. Omitted fields stay unchanged. Requires team-management permission; definitions in retired teams cannot be updated.

operation.summary: Exchanges a Google OAuth code, sets the authentication cookie, and returns workspace access details.
operation.description: Exchanges a Google OAuth code, sets the authentication cookie, and returns workspace access details. May create an account unless disallowSignup is true.

operation.summary: Copies an image from an external URL into Linear’s private upload storage.
operation.description: Copies an image from an external URL into Linear’s private upload storage. The URL must let Linear download the image directly; an HTML page containing the image is not accepted. On success, the returned URL refers to the copied image and can be used in Linear content. Unlike fileUpload, this mutation performs the download and upload for you.

operation.summary: Prepares a file in Linear’s import storage.
operation.description: Prepares a file in Linear’s import storage. Upload the raw bytes with HTTP PUT to the returned uploadUrl, using all returned headers and the matching Content-Type. The upload must start within one minute and contain exactly the declared number of bytes. Success prepares the destination; it does not upload the bytes or start an import.

operation.summary: Changes read or snooze state for the authenticated user’s group of related inbox notifications.
operation.description: Changes read or snooze state for the authenticated user’s group of related inbox notifications. Supply a notification UUID from the group and at least one state change. The response includes the requested notification and all notifications changed.

operation.summary: Adds an initiative label while keeping the other labels.
operation.description: Adds an initiative label while keeping the other labels. Label groups themselves cannot be applied, and the group’s selection rules still apply.

operation.summary: Archives an initiative.
Creates an initiative in a workspace where initiatives are enabled.
operation.description: Creates an initiative in a workspace where initiatives are enabled. You can assign an owner and lead team at creation. Add projects separately with initiativeToProjectCreate, and build a hierarchy with initiativeRelationCreate.

operation.summary: Moves an initiative to the trash instead of immediately deleting it permanently.
operation.description: Moves an initiative to the trash instead of immediately deleting it permanently. You can restore it with initiativeUnarchive while it remains available.

operation.summary: Creates a workspace label or label group for initiatives.
operation.description: Creates a workspace label or label group for initiatives. Requires workspace label-management permission. Use parentId to place a label in a group.

operation.summary: Deletes an initiative label and its children, removing their assignments from initiatives.
Restores a previously retired initiative label, making it available for use on new initiatives.
Retires an initiative label.
operation.description: Retires an initiative label. Retired labels remain on existing initiatives but cannot be applied to new ones.

operation.summary: Changes the supplied label fields.
operation.description: Changes the supplied label fields. Omitted fields stay unchanged. Requires workspace label-management permission.

operation.summary: Adds a child initiative to a parent.
operation.description: Adds a child initiative to a parent. Both must be accessible and unarchived, and the workspace must support sub-initiatives. When the new parent overlaps the child’s existing hierarchy, the overlapping parent links are removed as part of the move. Cycles and excessive nesting are rejected.

operation.summary: Removes a parent-child link without deleting either initiative.
operation.description: Removes a parent-child link without deleting either initiative. Deleting a link that no longer exists succeeds without making changes; an existing link still requires access to both initiatives.

operation.summary: Changes a child initiative’s ordering within its parent.
operation.description: Changes a child initiative’s ordering within its parent. The relation’s endpoints remain unchanged. Both initiatives must be visible to you.

operation.summary: Removes a label from the initiative while keeping its other labels.
operation.description: Removes a label from the initiative while keeping its other labels. The label itself is not deleted.

operation.summary: Links an accessible, active project to an accessible, active initiative.
operation.description: Links an accessible, active project to an accessible, active initiative. Neither may be read-only. The link is rejected if the project is already in that initiative or one of its ancestors or descendants. App users need initiative:write scope.

operation.summary: Removes an active project-to-initiative link without deleting either entity.
operation.description: Removes an active project-to-initiative link without deleting either entity. Requires access to the association; app users need initiative:write scope.

operation.summary: Changes the project’s sort order within the initiative.
operation.description: Changes the project’s sort order within the initiative. The initiative and project endpoints cannot be changed through this mutation.

operation.summary: Restores an archived or trashed initiative.
operation.description: Restores an archived or trashed initiative. This makes the existing initiative available again with its saved properties and associations.

operation.summary: Updates the supplied fields of an initiative you can access.
operation.description: Updates the supplied fields of an initiative you can access. Omitted fields keep their current values. Changing the lead team can change who can see the initiative, and the owner must be able to access the new team.

operation.summary: Archives an update and recalculates the initiative’s health from the remaining updates.
operation.description: Archives an update and recalculates the initiative’s health from the remaining updates. You must be the author or have permission to manage workspace entities. Use initiativeUpdateUnarchive to restore it.

operation.summary: Publishes an update, records the current user as author, captures the initiative’s projects, and refreshes its health.
operation.description: Publishes an update, records the current user as author, captures the initiative’s projects, and refreshes its health. Provide the written message in input.body.

operation.summary: Restores an archived update and recalculates the initiative’s health.
operation.description: Restores an archived update and recalculates the initiative’s health. You must be the author or have permission to manage workspace entities.

operation.summary: Edits an update’s message or health.
operation.description: Edits an update’s message or health. You must be the author or have permission to manage workspace entities. Editing the latest update while it is less than one hour old also refreshes its project snapshots.

operation.summary: Disconnects an integration that supports archiving while retaining its record for a later reconnect.
operation.description: Disconnects an integration that supports archiving while retaining its record for a later reconnect. You can archive your own personal connection; workspace connections generally require integration-creation permission. GitHub installation removal and Jira webhook cleanup run in the background, so a successful response can precede the completed disconnection. Services that do not support archiving must use integrationDelete instead.

operation.summary: Connects the public or private Slack channel selected during OAuth to an existing Asks integration.
operation.description: Connects the public or private Slack channel selected during OAuth to an existing Asks integration. The channel must be in that integration's Slack workspace and must not already be connected. Individual channel connections require full Asks access and permission to manage Asks settings. Check addBot after success and invite the bot manually when true. Direct messages work with Asks without this setup.

operation.summary: Disconnects an integration that supports deletion and removes its connection record.
operation.description: Disconnects an integration that supports deletion and removes its connection record. You can remove your own personal connection; workspace connections require integration-creation permission, and team, project, or view connections follow the permissions for that resource. Some services finish external cleanup in the background, so success does not guarantee that cleanup has finished. Services that retain a record for reconnecting must use integrationArchive instead.

operation.summary: Connects a Discord server using the OAuth code and redirect URI from its authorization flow, and links the authorizing Discord user to your Linear account.
operation.description: Connects a Discord server using the OAuth code and redirect URI from its authorization flow, and links the authorizing Discord user to your Linear account. A Linear workspace can have one Discord connection, and the Discord server cannot already belong to another Linear workspace's connection.

operation.summary: Connects Figma using an OAuth authorization code and its redirect URI, storing the credentials needed for the workspace integration.
operation.description: Connects Figma using an OAuth authorization code and its redirect URI, storing the credentials needed for the workspace integration. The workspace cannot already have an active Figma connection.

operation.summary: Connects Front using an OAuth grant.
operation.description: Connects Front using an OAuth grant. Requires the workspace's support integration plan feature and no existing Front connection. New connections initially reopen linked Front conversations when a Linear issue is completed or canceled; comments do not trigger reopening by default.

operation.summary: Starts a GitHub Enterprise Server connection for a GitHub organization or personal account.
operation.description: Starts a GitHub Enterprise Server connection for a GitHub organization or personal account. Open setupUrl to register the app, configure it with webhookSecret, then use installUrl to install it. Call verifyGitHubEnterpriseServerInstallation to check that the app has connected. Success here means the setup record was saved, not that installation is complete. An archived connection for the same organization is reused.

operation.summary: Links your GitHub account using an OAuth code from Linear's GitHub App authorization flow.
operation.description: Links your GitHub account using an OAuth code from Linear's GitHub App authorization flow. codeAccess selects the app with repository code access and defaults to false. This is a personal account connection; connecting a workspace's GitHub App installation uses integrationGithubConnect.

operation.summary: Creates the workspace's GitHub commit integration and returns its webhook secret.
operation.description: Creates the workspace's GitHub commit integration and returns its webhook secret. Use the secret when configuring the webhook in GitHub; creating this record alone does not configure GitHub to send events.

operation.summary: Connects a GitHub App installation to the workspace using its installation ID and OAuth grant.
operation.description: Connects a GitHub App installation to the workspace using its installation ID and OAuth grant. If replacing a connection would make repositories used by GitHub Issues sync inaccessible, the call stops and returns gitHub.lostRepositoryNames. Review that list, then repeat with confirmReplace set to true to accept the change. GitHub Enterprise Cloud connections require the corresponding workspace plan feature.

operation.summary: Connects the GitHub Import App installation authorized by the supplied OAuth code.
operation.description: Connects the GitHub Import App installation authorized by the supplied OAuth code. This creates the connection used to discover repositories for import; it does not import issues by itself.

operation.summary: Queues a refresh of repositories and labels available to a GitHub import integration.
operation.description: Queues a refresh of repositories and labels available to a GitHub import integration. Success confirms scheduling.

operation.summary: Removes repository code access from a GitHub connection.
operation.description: Removes repository code access from a GitHub connection. Check action in the response: Done means the change is complete, while InstallBasicApp means you need to finish installing the basic GitHub App before setup is complete.

operation.summary: Connects a GitLab instance after checking its access token.
operation.description: Connects a GitLab instance after checking its access token. Configure the GitLab webhook with the returned webhookSecret after a successful response. Only one GitLab connection is allowed per workspace. Token or connectivity failures return success=false and diagnostic error fields instead of creating a connection.

operation.summary: Rotates the GitLab token, revoking the previous token and saving its replacement.
Tests the stored access token against a self-hosted GitLab instance, using the validation project when one is configured.
operation.description: Tests the stored access token against a self-hosted GitLab instance, using the validation project when one is configured. A successful check clears the connection's authentication and transient failure state. On failure, inspect success and the error fields for provider or proxy diagnostics. This mutation does not support the GitLab.com OAuth connection.

operation.summary: Enables or disables automatic self-rotation of the GitLab token.
Replaces a GitLab integration's access token after validating the replacement against its existing host and validation project.
operation.description: Replaces a GitLab integration's access token after validating the replacement against its existing host and validation project. The connection and webhook stay in place. Supply readonly and expiresAt when the instance cannot report that token information.

operation.summary: Connects Gong using an OAuth authorization code and its redirect URI.
operation.description: Connects Gong using an OAuth authorization code and its redirect URI. Requires the workspace's Gong integration plan feature and integration-creation permission. The workspace cannot already have an active Gong connection.

operation.summary: Connects Google Sheets using an OAuth grant that includes both access and refresh tokens.
operation.description: Connects Google Sheets using an OAuth grant that includes both access and refresh tokens. The workspace can have one active Google Sheets connection. This call saves the connection; use refreshGoogleSheetsData to request an export refresh.

operation.summary: Connects an Intercom workspace using an OAuth code and the redirect URI used during authorization.
operation.description: Connects an Intercom workspace using an OAuth code and the redirect URI used during authorization. The workspace needs access to the support integration plan feature. Reconnecting the same Intercom workspace refreshes credentials and keeps its settings; disconnect first to switch to a different Intercom workspace. An Intercom workspace cannot be connected to another Linear workspace at the same time.

operation.summary: Uninstalls the Intercom connection and removes its Linear record.
operation.description: Uninstalls the Intercom connection and removes its Linear record. It also completes local cleanup when access was already revoked in Intercom. Calling this after the Linear connection has been removed returns an error.

operation.summary: [DEPRECATED] Updates settings on the Intercom integration.
operation.description:
[DEPRECATED] Updates settings on the Intercom integration.

Deprecated: Manage Intercom integration settings in Linear workspace settings.

operation.summary: Links your Jira account to an existing workspace Jira integration.
operation.description: Links your Jira account to an existing workspace Jira integration. Supply either the OAuth authorization code for Jira Cloud or a personal access token for Jira Server. When the workspace has more than one possible Jira connection, supply workspaceIntegrationId to choose which one to link.

operation.summary: Enables Loom integration for the workspace.
operation.description:
Enables Loom integration for the workspace.

Deprecated: Not available.

operation.summary: Links your Microsoft account to Linear.
operation.description: Links your Microsoft account to Linear. Its tenant must already be connected through a workspace Microsoft Teams integration. Reconnecting the same account refreshes credentials when the existing personal connection has an authentication error; otherwise, disconnect the existing personal connection before linking another account.

operation.summary: Connects the Microsoft tenant identified by the OAuth grant to this Linear workspace.
operation.description: Connects the Microsoft tenant identified by the OAuth grant to this Linear workspace. An archived connection to the same tenant is restored. Multiple tenants require the corresponding plan feature, and a tenant cannot be actively connected to another Linear workspace. Personal Microsoft accounts are linked separately with integrationMicrosoftPersonalConnect.

operation.summary: Records interest in an integration that is not currently available.
operation.description: Records interest in an integration that is not currently available. No authentication is required, and this does not create an integration or start an installation. Success means the request was accepted for analytics; it does not promise that the integration will be built.

operation.summary: Connects Salesforce using an OAuth grant and verifies that the authorizing user can access the Linear managed package, including its required license.
operation.description: Connects Salesforce using an OAuth grant and verifies that the authorizing user can access the Linear managed package, including its required license. Requires the workspace's enterprise integration plan feature. Reconnecting an active connection to the same subdomain refreshes credentials while keeping settings and templates; restoring an archived connection runs setup again. Disconnect first to switch to a different Salesforce subdomain.

operation.summary: Connects a Sentry installation by exchanging its grant code and confirming installation with Sentry.
operation.description: Connects a Sentry installation by exchanging its grant code and confirming installation with Sentry. The workspace can have one active Sentry connection. The new connection initially enables completing linked Linear issues when Sentry issues are resolved and reopening them when Sentry issues are unresolved.

operation.summary: Connects a Slack workspace to the main Linear Slack app using an OAuth grant.
operation.description: Connects a Slack workspace to the main Linear Slack app using an OAuth grant. Reconnecting an archived connection restores it with fresh credentials. Connecting multiple Slack workspaces requires the corresponding plan feature; the same Slack workspace cannot have two active connections or belong to another Linear workspace's connection.

operation.summary: Connects a Slack workspace to the Linear Asks app for issue intake.
operation.description: Connects a Slack workspace to the Linear Asks app for issue intake. Requires a workspace plan with Asks access. An archived connection to the same Slack workspace is restored with fresh credentials. Multiple Slack workspaces require the corresponding plan feature, and each Slack workspace can be connected to Asks in only one Linear workspace.

operation.summary: Connects the Slack channel selected during OAuth to a custom view and creates default notification settings if needed.
operation.description: Connects the Slack channel selected during OAuth to a custom view and creates default notification settings if needed. You must be able to edit the view, and the view cannot already have this type of Slack connection. Check the response for remaining bot or workspace setup.

operation.summary: Links a customer to a public or private Slack channel in a connected Asks workspace.
operation.description: Links a customer to a public or private Slack channel in a connected Asks workspace. Both the customer and channel must be unlinked.

operation.summary: Queues an import of custom emoji from Slack using the OAuth grant.
operation.description: Queues an import of custom emoji from Slack using the OAuth grant. Success confirms scheduling.

operation.summary: Fetches the current Slack workspace name and updates the name stored on an active Slack or Asks integration.
operation.description: Fetches the current Slack workspace name and updates the name stored on an active Slack or Asks integration. This refreshes Linear's display name; it does not rename the workspace in Slack. A valid integration token is required.

operation.summary: Connects the Slack channel selected during OAuth to receive project updates from across the workspace.
operation.description: Connects the Slack channel selected during OAuth to receive project updates from across the workspace. Requires integration-management permission. Check addBot and the nudge fields in the response for any remaining Slack setup.

operation.summary: Links your Slack account for personal notifications and opens a direct message with the Linear app.
operation.description: Links your Slack account for personal notifications and opens a direct message with the Linear app. The Slack workspace must already have a Slack or Asks connection. You can have one active personal Slack connection, and the same Slack account cannot be linked to another user in this Linear workspace. An archived connection owned by you can be restored.

operation.summary: Connects the Slack channel selected during OAuth to a Linear team and creates its default notification settings if needed.
operation.description: Connects the Slack channel selected during OAuth to a Linear team and creates its default notification settings if needed. Requires permission to manage the team, and each team can have one such connection. Direct messages are not supported. Check addBot and the nudge fields in the response for any remaining Slack setup.

operation.summary: Connects the Slack channel selected during OAuth to a project you can access.
operation.description: Connects the Slack channel selected during OAuth to a project you can access. Choose notifications for project notifications or updates for project updates; each service can have one connection per project. The call also links the channel to the project and creates default notification settings if needed. Check the response for remaining bot or workspace setup.

operation.summary: Makes an issue template available through Slack Asks, Slack, Intercom, Zendesk, or Salesforce.
operation.description: Makes an issue template available through Slack Asks, Slack, Intercom, Zendesk, or Salesforce. Slack Asks requires permission to manage Asks, a connected intake destination, and a team template; linking the template enables triage for that team. Other supported integrations require integration-management permission and accept up to ten templates. Private-team templates are supported only by Slack Asks.

operation.summary: Removes a template's link to an integration or intake destination.
operation.description: Removes a template's link to an integration or intake destination. The template itself and the integration remain available. Requires permission to manage the Asks integration for Slack Asks, or integration-management permission for other services.

operation.summary: Connects Zendesk using an OAuth grant and creates or selects the user that authors internal notes.
operation.description: Connects Zendesk using an OAuth grant and creates or selects the user that authors internal notes. Requires the workspace's support integration plan feature. Reconnecting the same subdomain refreshes credentials and keeps existing settings; an archived connection is restored. Disconnect the current integration before switching to a different Zendesk subdomain.

operation.summary: Creates notification preferences for a destination you can access, with edit permission required for custom views.
operation.description: Creates notification preferences for a destination you can access, with edit permission required for custom views. Supply exactly one team, project, initiative, or view. Settings must not already exist for that destination and, for team settings, context view; use integrationsSettingsUpdate when they do. An app writing initiative preferences also needs initiative:write scope.

operation.summary: Updates the event preferences on an existing integration settings record.
operation.description: Updates the event preferences on an existing integration settings record. Only supplied booleans change, and the destination stays the same. Custom-view settings require permission to edit the view; apps changing initiative settings need initiative:write scope. For older settings that combined update and comment notifications, the first edit preserves the previous comment preference independently.

operation.summary: Add a label without replacing the issue’s existing labels.
operation.description: Add a label without replacing the issue’s existing labels. The label must be available to the issue’s team.

operation.summary: Archives an issue and its sub-issues, keeping their data available for later restoration.
operation.description: Archives an issue and its sub-issues, keeping their data available for later restoration. Archived issues are excluded from normal issue lists. Pass trash only when you want the deletion grace period to apply instead.

operation.summary: Creates one to 50 issues in a single batch.
operation.description: Creates one to 50 issues in a single batch. If any creation fails, none of the issues in the batch are saved. Put parent inputs before their sub-issues and supply parent UUIDs to connect issues created in the same batch.

operation.summary: Applies the same update input to one to 50 issues.
operation.description: Applies the same update input to one to 50 issues. The batch runs as one transaction, so a failed update rolls back the other updates. Use the returned issues to read the resulting values.

operation.summary: Creates an issue in the chosen team and returns it with its assigned identifier.
operation.description: Creates an issue in the chosen team and returns it with its assigned identifier. You can supply a template to populate defaults and create any sub-issues it defines. Team settings and automation may set values such as the initial status, assignee, and cycle.

operation.summary: Moves an issue to the trash and trashes its unarchived sub-issues that you can access.
operation.description: Moves an issue to the trash and trashes its unarchived sub-issues that you can access. Trashed issues can be restored during the 30-day grace period; permanentlyDelete skips that period and requires workspace entity-management permission.

operation.summary: Stop syncing an issue with the Jira or GitHub integration identified by its sync attachment.
Starts fetching Asana tasks into an asynchronous import job.
operation.description: Starts fetching Asana tasks into an asynchronous import job. Choose an existing destination team or a new team name. Configure the fetched data and call issueImportProcess to create Linear records.

operation.summary: Creates an asynchronous import from a Jira CSV already uploaded to the workspace’s import storage.
operation.description: Creates an asynchronous import from a Jira CSV already uploaded to the workspace’s import storage. Choose an existing destination team or a new team name. The response accepts the job; it does not mean the imported records are ready.

operation.summary: Starts fetching stories from Shortcut, whose legacy API name is clubhouse, into an asynchronous import job.
operation.description: Starts fetching stories from Shortcut, whose legacy API name is clubhouse, into an asynchronous import job. Choose an existing destination team or a new team name. Configure the fetched data and call issueImportProcess to create Linear records.

operation.summary: Starts fetching GitHub issues into an asynchronous import job.
operation.description: Starts fetching GitHub issues into an asynchronous import job. Choose an existing destination team or provide a name for a new one, and repositories the workspace can import from. After fetching and configuration, use issueImportProcess to create the Linear records. Requires workspace import permission.

operation.summary: Starts fetching Jira issues into an asynchronous import job.
operation.description: Starts fetching Jira issues into an asynchronous import job. Choose an existing destination team or a new team name and the source Jira project. After fetching and configuration, use issueImportProcess to create the Linear records. Requires workspace import permission.

operation.summary: Schedules deletion of an import and the data it created, then returns the job with status deleting.
operation.description: Schedules deletion of an import and the data it created, then returns the job with status deleting. This is available within 14 days for eligible imports awaiting configuration, completed imports, or failed imports. You must be the creator or an admin with the destination team’s deletion permission, and another import from the same service must not be processing.

operation.summary: Saves the supplied mappings and schedules creation of Linear records from the fetched source data.
operation.description: Saves the supplied mappings and schedules creation of Linear records from the fetched source data. Fails without saving the mappings when an external-service import has not finished fetching its source data. The import must be inProgress; otherwise the mappings are saved but success is false. A successful response means processing was accepted, not that it has finished. Linear-to-Linear migrations can only be managed from the Linear app.

operation.summary: Saves mapping choices without starting the import.
operation.description: Saves mapping choices without starting the import. For external-service imports, supply the full replacement mapping, and wait until the import has fetched its source data. Requires workspace import permission; Linear-to-Linear migrations can only be managed from the Linear app.

operation.summary: Create a workspace or team label.
operation.description: Create a workspace or team label. Requires permission to manage labels in its scope.

operation.summary: Deletes a label and its inherited copies.
operation.description: Deletes a label and its inherited copies. Assignments to that label are removed from issues in the background, so they may remain visible briefly after the mutation succeeds. Retire a label instead if you want to preserve its existing assignments.

operation.summary: Makes a retired label available for new assignments again.
operation.description: Makes a retired label available for new assignments again. Existing issue assignments are preserved. Restoring a group also restores its child labels.

operation.summary: Retires a label so it cannot be newly assigned, while keeping it on issues that already use it.
operation.description: Retires a label so it cannot be newly assigned, while keeping it on issues that already use it. Retiring a group also retires its children. Use issueLabelRestore to make the label available again.

operation.summary: Update a label.
operation.description: Update a label. Requires permission to manage labels in its scope; inherited labels must be edited at their source.

operation.summary: Creates a relationship between two issues, replacing any conflicting relation between the pair and reusing an identical one.
operation.description: Creates a relationship between two issues, replacing any conflicting relation between the pair and reusing an identical one. A duplicate relation closes the source as a duplicate of the target and can move linked customer requests to the target. You must have access to both issues and any permissions required for the merge.

operation.summary: Removes a relation by its UUID.
operation.description: Removes a relation by its UUID. Removing a duplicate relation also runs the unmerge behavior, including moving customer requests back to the original issue when applicable.

operation.summary: Changes a relation’s type or the issues it connects.
operation.description: Changes a relation’s type or the issues it connects. Omitted fields are unchanged, and an issue cannot relate to itself. Changing to or from duplicate also applies the corresponding merge or unmerge behavior.

operation.summary: Creates a reminder notification for you at reminderAt.
operation.description: Creates a reminder notification for you at reminderAt. The time must be in the future, and existing reminders for this issue are replaced. The payload returns success without an issue object.

operation.summary: Remove one label while keeping the issue’s other labels.
Shares an issue with a user who would not otherwise be able to access it.
operation.description: Shares an issue with a user who would not otherwise be able to access it. The viewer must have native access to the issue's full sub-issue tree and permission to share issues in the issue's team. Issues that inherit sharing from a parent issue cannot be shared directly.

operation.summary: Subscribes a user to issue updates.
operation.description: Subscribes a user to issue updates. Omit both userId and userEmail to subscribe yourself, or provide one of them to choose another workspace user. Subscribing an existing subscriber leaves the subscription in place.

operation.summary: Associates an issue with a release and returns the link.
operation.description: Associates an issue with a release and returns the link. The issue must be editable and both resources accessible; release management must be available in the workspace. If the association already exists, the mutation returns an error rather than reusing it.

operation.summary: Removes an issue-to-release association by the link’s UUID, keeping the issue and release.
operation.description: Removes an issue-to-release association by the link’s UUID, keeping the issue and release. The issue must be editable and the release accessible. Returns an error when the link does not exist.

operation.summary: Removes the association between the specified issue and release, keeping both resources.
operation.description: Removes the association between the specified issue and release, keeping both resources. The issue must be editable and the release accessible. Returns an error when the association does not exist.

operation.summary: Restores an archived issue and its sub-issues to normal issue lists.
operation.description: Restores an archived issue and its sub-issues to normal issue lists. Automatic-archive markers are cleared, and a project association is removed if the project no longer includes the issue’s team.

operation.summary: Stops sharing an issue with a user.
operation.description: Stops sharing an issue with a user. The viewer must have native access to the issue's full sub-issue tree and permission to share issues in the issue's team. Issues that inherit sharing from a parent issue cannot be unshared directly.

operation.summary: Removes a user’s subscription to issue updates.
operation.description: Removes a user’s subscription to issue updates. Omit both userId and userEmail to unsubscribe yourself, or provide one of them to choose another workspace user.

operation.summary: Updates an issue by UUID or human-readable identifier and returns its resulting values.
operation.description: Updates an issue by UUID or human-readable identifier and returns its resulting values. Omitted fields keep their values; list inputs replace their existing lists unless an add/remove field is used. Changes can also trigger team workflow behavior, such as automatic cycle assignment.

operation.summary: Imports or syncs up to 50 projects from one connected Jira site.
operation.description: Imports or syncs up to 50 projects from one connected Jira site. When both are requested, sync starts after import. Projects are checked independently; retry failed projects only. Repeating an unchanged, running migration returns its existing records. Imports into one team run sequentially. Requires the `admin` scope, access to destination teams, and import permission when importing.

operation.summary: Signs out the current session and clears authentication cookies.
operation.description: Signs out the current session and clears authentication cookies. If the token has no session ID, signs out all sessions for the account.

operation.summary: Signs out all sessions for the account, including the current session, and clears authentication cookies.
Signs out every other session for the authenticated account while keeping the current session active.
Revokes one sign-in session belonging to the authenticated account.
operation.description: Revokes one sign-in session belonging to the authenticated account. Use an ID returned by authenticationSessions; it may be the current session or another device's session. Requires session JWT authentication.

operation.summary: Archives one of your notifications, removing it from the active inbox.
operation.description: Archives one of your notifications, removing it from the active inbox. Other notifications in the same group remain unchanged. Use notificationArchiveAll to archive the group.

operation.summary: Archives the authenticated user’s active notifications for the selected entity or notification group.
Subscribes to or unsubscribes from a specific notification category for a given notification channel.
operation.description: Subscribes to or unsubscribes from a specific notification category for a given notification channel. For example, subscribe to 'issueAssignment' notifications via the 'email' channel.

operation.summary: Marks the authenticated user’s active notifications for the selected entity or notification group as read.
Marks the authenticated user’s active notifications for the selected entity or notification group as unread.
Snoozes the authenticated user’s active notifications for the selected entity or notification group.
Subscribes the authenticated user to one target and its requested notification types.
operation.description: Subscribes the authenticated user to one target and its requested notification types. Rejects an existing subscription to the same target and view.

operation.summary: Deletes a notification subscription reference.
operation.description:
Deletes a notification subscription reference.

Deprecated: Update `notificationSubscription.active` to `false` instead.

operation.summary: Updates a subscription owned by the authenticated user.
operation.description: Updates a subscription owned by the authenticated user. Use active: false to pause it without deleting its configuration, or replace notificationSubscriptionTypes to change the events you follow. Subscriptions to read-only projects cannot be changed.

operation.summary: Restores one of your archived notifications.
operation.description: Restores one of your archived notifications. Its read and snooze states are preserved, so a snoozed notification may still be absent from the visible inbox.

operation.summary: Unsnoozes the authenticated user’s active notifications for the selected entity or notification group.
Updates one of the authenticated user’s notifications.
operation.description: Updates one of the authenticated user’s notifications. Related notifications are unchanged.

operation.summary: [ALPHA] Archives an OAuth application created by the calling OAuth application.
[ALPHA] Creates an OAuth application private to the current workspace and managed by the calling OAuth application.
operation.description: [ALPHA] Creates an OAuth application private to the current workspace and managed by the calling OAuth application. The caller needs workspace API management permission. Save clientSecret and any webhookSecret from the first successful response. Retrying with the same idempotency key returns the existing unarchived application without updating it and with secrets omitted. Use the application’s id for later management operations and clientId for OAuth flows.

operation.summary: [ALPHA] Replaces the client secret for an application created by the caller and returns the new secret.
operation.description: [ALPHA] Replaces the client secret for an application created by the caller and returns the new secret. Store it before discarding the response; it cannot be retrieved later. The old secret stops working at once, as does a previous secret that a planned rotation kept working. Tokens issued through client_credentials are revoked, while tokens from the authorization-code flow remain valid. The caller must be able to manage the application’s credentials, including its private-team access, as well as have workspace API management permission.

operation.summary: [ALPHA] Rotates the webhook signing secret for an OAuth application created by the calling OAuth application.
[ALPHA] Updates an unarchived application created by the calling OAuth application in this workspace.
operation.description: [ALPHA] Updates an unarchived application created by the calling OAuth application in this workspace. Omitted fields keep their current values. Enabling client_credentials or changing the webhook destination requires access to every private team available to the app, or workspace owner permission; an app with access to all private teams requires an owner. Workspace API management permission is required for every update.

operation.summary: Cancels a scheduled workspace deletion while the deletion process still permits cancellation.
operation.description: Cancels a scheduled workspace deletion while the deletion process still permits cancellation. Requires workspace-settings permission.

operation.summary: Schedules deletion of the workspace and its data after validating the code from organizationDeleteChallenge.
operation.description: Schedules deletion of the workspace and its data after validating the code from organizationDeleteChallenge. This does not finish the deletion during the request. Use organizationCancelDelete while cancellation is still available.

operation.summary: Requests a deletion confirmation code for the workspace.
operation.description: Requests a deletion confirmation code for the workspace. The code is sent to the requesting user's email and must be used with the organizationDelete mutation to confirm deletion.

operation.summary: Removes a domain configuration from the workspace and its authentication settings.
operation.description: Removes a domain configuration from the workspace and its authentication settings. Requires workspace-settings permission. Other domain configurations for the workspace are unchanged.

operation.summary: Invites an email address to the workspace and sends an invitation email.
operation.description: Invites an email address to the workspace and sends an invitation email. Your role and workspace invitation settings must allow the requested role and teams. Guest invitations require teams; an existing user or unexpired invitation for the address causes an error.

operation.summary: Deletes (archives) a workspace invite, preventing it from being accepted.
Replaces the teams an invitee will join on acceptance.
operation.description: Replaces the teams an invitee will join on acceptance. Requires permission to manage invitations, and the selected teams must be valid for the invite’s role. This does not change the invitee’s email or role.

operation.summary: [DEPRECATED] Starts a trial for the workspace.
operation.description:
[DEPRECATED] Starts a trial for the workspace.

Deprecated: Use organizationStartTrialForPlan

operation.summary: Starts a trial for the workspace on the specified plan type.
operation.description: Starts a trial for the workspace on the specified plan type. The workspace must not already be on a paid plan or in an active trial.

operation.summary: Updates the workspace associated with your credentials.
operation.description: Updates the workspace associated with your credentials. Omitted fields keep their current values. Most changes require workspace-settings permission; project and initiative reminder schedules require schedule-management permission. Some settings also depend on the workspace’s plan.

operation.summary: Adds a project label while keeping the project’s other labels.
operation.description: Adds a project label while keeping the project’s other labels. The label must be available to the project; label-group and team-scoping rules still apply.

operation.summary: Archives a project.
operation.description:
Archives a project.

Deprecated: Deprecated in favor of projectDelete.

operation.summary: Creates a project in the supplied teams.
operation.description: Creates a project in the supplied teams. You can apply a project template to fill in defaults and create its milestones, initial issues, and initiative associations. The new project must have at least one accessible team.

operation.summary: Moves a project to the trash.
operation.description: Moves a project to the trash. This archives the project rather than immediately deleting it permanently. You can restore it with projectUnarchive while it remains available in the trash.

operation.summary: Disables external sync on a project.
Creates a label or label group for projects.
operation.description: Creates a label or label group for projects. Workspace labels require workspace label-management permission; team labels require label-management permission in that team and a plan that supports team project labels. replaceTeamLabels can migrate matching labels into the new scope.

operation.summary: Deletes a project label, its children, and inherited copies, removing their assignments from projects.
Restores a previously retired project label, making it available for use on new projects.
Retires a project label.
operation.description: Retires a project label. Retired labels remain on existing projects but cannot be applied to new ones.

operation.summary: Updates the supplied project-label fields and propagates changes to inherited copies.
operation.description: Updates the supplied project-label fields and propagates changes to inherited copies. Requires label-management permission for the label’s workspace or team. Update the source label rather than an inherited copy.

operation.summary: Creates a milestone in a project you can edit.
operation.description: Creates a milestone in a project you can edit. Its name must be unique among the project’s active milestones. A milestone starts without issues; assign issues to it separately.

operation.summary: Permanently deletes a milestone from a project you can edit.
operation.description: Permanently deletes a milestone from a project you can edit. The issues are kept in the project, but their milestone association is removed.

operation.summary: Moves a milestone and its issues to another project, including archived issues.
operation.description: Moves a milestone and its issues to another project, including archived issues. The caller must have access to every issue in the milestone, and the milestone and destination project must be writable. If an issue's team is not part of the destination project, provide newIssueTeamId or addIssueTeamToProject. The returned team snapshots can be passed to the undo inputs when moving the milestone back to its original project.

operation.summary: Updates a milestone in a project you can edit, including an archived milestone.
operation.description: Updates a milestone in a project you can edit, including an archived milestone. Omitted fields keep their current values. Changing projectId moves the milestone and clears its links from issue drafts in the previous project.

operation.summary: Creates a dependency between two different projects using date or milestone anchors.
Deletes the dependency without deleting either project or milestone.
Updates the supplied dependency fields and validates both project endpoints.
Removes a project label while keeping the project’s other labels.
operation.description: Removes a project label while keeping the project’s other labels. The label itself is not deleted.

operation.summary: Archives a project status.
operation.description: Archives a project status. The status must not have any active projects assigned to it and must not be the last status of its type.

operation.summary: Creates a new project status.
Unarchives a project status.
Updates a project status.
Restores an archived or trashed project.
operation.description: Restores an archived or trashed project. The operation checks the project quota of each associated team before restoring it.

operation.summary: Updates the supplied fields of a project you can edit.
operation.description: Updates the supplied fields of a project you can edit. Omitted fields keep their current values. List inputs such as memberIds and labelIds replace the corresponding lists; see each input for clearing rules and team-access behavior.

operation.summary: Archives an update and recalculates the project’s health from the remaining updates.
operation.description: Archives an update and recalculates the project’s health from the remaining updates. You must be the author or have permission to manage workspace entities. Use projectUpdateUnarchive to restore it.

operation.summary: Publishes a status update for a project you can edit.
operation.description: Publishes a status update for a project you can edit. The update records the current user as author, captures project progress, and refreshes the project’s health. Provide the message in input.body.

operation.summary: Archives a project update and recalculates project health.
operation.description:
