Archives a project update and recalculates project health. Use projectUpdateUnarchive to restore it.

Deprecated: Use `projectUpdateArchive` instead.

operation.summary: Restores an archived update and recalculates the project’s health.
operation.description: Restores an archived update and recalculates the project’s health. The update must currently be archived, and you must be its author or have permission to manage workspace entities.

operation.summary: Edits an update’s message or health.
operation.description: Edits an update’s message or health. You must be its author or have permission to manage workspace entities. Editing the latest update while it is less than one hour old also refreshes its progress snapshot.

operation.summary: Registers a browser or device to receive push notifications for the authenticated user.
operation.description: Registers a browser or device to receive push notifications for the authenticated user. If the same subscription data is already registered, returns that record; otherwise replaces the subscription associated with the current sign-in session. userId in the input is ignored. Successful registration does not guarantee notification delivery; use pushSubscriptionTest to request a test notification.

operation.summary: Deletes a push subscription to stop sending notifications through it.
operation.description: Deletes a push subscription to stop sending notifications through it. Select success to confirm deletion. This operation does not populate entity, so selecting that field produces a GraphQL error.

operation.summary: Adds an emoji reaction as you to one issue, comment, or update.
operation.description: Adds an emoji reaction as you to one issue, comment, or update. If you already used that emoji on the same resource, the existing reaction is returned. You must be allowed to comment on the target.

operation.summary: Removes a reaction by its UUID and updates the target’s reaction summary.
operation.description: Removes a reaction by its UUID and updates the target’s reaction summary. You must be its creator or have workspace permission to manage entities, and you must be allowed to comment on the target.

operation.summary: Queues a Google Sheets export refresh.
operation.description: Queues a Google Sheets export refresh. Success confirms scheduling; the returned integration may still contain the previous export state.

operation.summary: Archives a release.
Completes the release identified by pipeline and version, or the latest started release when version is omitted.
operation.description: Completes the release identified by pipeline and version, or the latest started release when version is omitted. Completing a scheduled release may move its open issues to the next release, according to the pipeline’s rollover setting.

operation.summary: Marks a release as completed using an access key.
operation.description: Marks a release as completed using an access key. If version is provided, completes that specific release; otherwise completes the most recent started release. The pipeline is inferred from the access key.

operation.summary: Creates a new release in a pipeline.
operation.description: Creates a new release in a pipeline. If no stage is specified, defaults to the first completed stage for continuous pipelines or the first started stage for scheduled pipelines.

operation.summary: Moves a release to trash for permanent deletion after the retention period.
operation.description: Moves a release to trash for permanent deletion after the retention period. Use releaseUnarchive to restore it before deletion.

operation.summary: Creates a note covering releases from one pipeline.
operation.description: Creates a note covering releases from one pipeline. Supply explicit release IDs or an inclusive range, plus an optional title and Markdown body. A scheduled pipeline’s note must cover exactly one release.

operation.summary: Permanently deletes a release note and its body.
operation.description: Permanently deletes a release note and its body. The covered releases remain.

operation.summary: Updates a release note’s title, body, or covered releases.
operation.description: Updates a release note’s title, body, or covered releases. Omitted fields remain unchanged, and a new release selection replaces the old one. The note stays in its original pipeline.

operation.summary: Archives a pipeline and schedules archival of its releases.
operation.description: Archives a pipeline and schedules archival of its releases. The release changes run in the background, so they may not be complete when this mutation returns. Requires workspace team-management permission or ownership of every associated team.

operation.summary: Creates a release pipeline with default stages, subject to your workspace’s plan and quota.
operation.description: Creates a release pipeline with default stages, subject to your workspace’s plan and quota. Requires workspace team-management permission or ownership of every team associated with the pipeline.

operation.summary: Moves a pipeline and its releases to the trash for permanent deletion after the retention period.
operation.description: Moves a pipeline and its releases to the trash for permanent deletion after the retention period. Repeating the operation does not extend that period. Requires workspace team-management permission or ownership of every associated team.

operation.summary: Restores a pipeline and schedules restoration of its archived releases.
operation.description: Restores a pipeline and schedules restoration of its archived releases. Individually trashed releases are left in the trash. The release changes run in the background, and the same pipeline administration permissions apply.

operation.summary: Updates an existing release pipeline.
operation.description: Updates an existing release pipeline. Supports updating name, slug, type, production flag, path patterns, and team associations. Private teams that the current user cannot access are preserved in the team list.

operation.summary: Archives a release stage.
operation.description: Archives a release stage. Only started-type stages can be archived, and only if they have no active releases and at least one other stage of the same type remains. Cannot archive the last non-frozen started stage.

operation.summary: Creates a new release stage in a pipeline.
operation.description: Creates a new release stage in a pipeline. Non-started stages must use default names and colors and are unique by type; creating a canonical duplicate returns the existing stage. Started stages can optionally be frozen, but at least one non-frozen started stage must remain.

operation.summary: Unarchives a release stage.
Updates an existing release stage.
operation.description: Updates an existing release stage. Only started-type stages can be edited. Supports updating name, color, position, and frozen status.

operation.summary: Associates issues found in issue or pull request references with a release.
operation.description: Associates issues found in issue or pull request references with a release. Continuous pipelines create completed releases and reuse an existing version only when its commit SHA matches. Scheduled pipelines accumulate issues in an open release or use the supplied version. Existing issue associations are kept unless explicitly reverted in a scheduled pipeline.

operation.summary: Syncs release data using an access key for CI/CD integration.
operation.description: Syncs release data using an access key for CI/CD integration. The pipeline is automatically inferred from the access key's configured resources, so no pipeline ID is needed in the input.

operation.summary: Restores an archived or trashed release before it is permanently deleted.
operation.description: Restores an archived or trashed release before it is permanently deleted. The release keeps its pipeline and saved issue associations.

operation.summary: Updates a release by ID.
operation.description: Updates a release by ID. Omitted fields remain unchanged. A release cannot move to another pipeline.

operation.summary: Updates a release by pipeline identifier.
operation.description: Updates a release by pipeline identifier. Finds the release by version, otherwise the latest started release or else the planned release with the earliest target date, and optionally transitions it to a new stage by name.

operation.summary: Updates a release by pipeline using an access key.
Re-sends a workspace invitation email for the specified invite ID.
Re-sends a workspace invitation email to the specified email address, if an outstanding invite exists for that address.

operation.summary: Completes SAML sign-in with the email and token issued by the SAML flow, then sets the authentication cookie.
operation.description: Completes SAML sign-in with the email and token issued by the SAML flow, then sets the authentication cookie. The response identifies workspace memberships and any workspaces that require a different sign-in method. Unlike email token sign-in, this operation does not require clientAuthCode.

operation.summary: Creates a team with workflow states, labels, and other initial resources.
operation.description: Creates a team with workflow states, labels, and other initial resources. You become a member and, for private teams or plans that support team owners, an owner. copySettingsFromTeamId copies settings and related resources from an existing team; copied settings take precedence over input values except an explicit private value.

operation.summary: Permanently deletes all cycles for a team and disables cycles.
operation.description: Permanently deletes all cycles for a team and disables cycles. Issues are kept, but their cycle associations are removed. Requires permission to manage the team.

operation.summary: Archives a team and schedules permanent deletion after a 30-day grace period.
operation.description: Archives a team and schedules permanent deletion after a 30-day grace period. You cannot delete the workspace’s final active team. Requires a workspace administrator or team owner; use teamUnarchive before deletion begins to restore it.

operation.summary: Deletes a previously used team key.
operation.description: Deletes a previously used team key. The active team key (the team's current key) cannot be deleted.

operation.summary: Adds a user to an active team after checking permission and membership limits.
operation.description: Adds a user to an active team after checking permission and membership limits. Regular workspace members also join ancestor teams. The operation fails if the user is already a member or if the team is archived, retired, or managed through SCIM.

operation.summary: Removes a user from a team after checking removal permissions and membership restrictions.
operation.description: Removes a user from a team after checking removal permissions and membership restrictions. Leaving cannot remove the user’s last active team, and SCIM-managed memberships must be managed through the identity provider. alsoLeaveParentTeams can extend the removal to parent teams.

operation.summary: Updates the team’s position in the member’s team list.
Restores an archived team and cancels its scheduled deletion while the grace period still permits cancellation.
operation.description: Restores an archived team and cancels its scheduled deletion while the grace period still permits cancellation. Requires workspace team-management permission, access to the team, and capacity for another active team on the workspace’s plan.

operation.summary: Updates the supplied team fields.
operation.description: Updates the supplied team fields. Changes require the relevant team-management permissions.

operation.summary: Create a template.
operation.description: Create a template. Requires permission to manage templates in the workspace, team, or release pipeline that owns it.

operation.summary: Deletes a template and its inherited copies.
operation.description: Deletes a template and its inherited copies. Requires permission to manage templates in its scope; inherited copies must be deleted at their source. Resources already created from the template remain.

operation.summary: Changes a template’s metadata, saved defaults, or team scope.
operation.description: Changes a template’s metadata, saved defaults, or team scope. Update an inherited template at its source, and supply the full templateData when replacing its configuration. Changing a template does not rewrite resources already created from it.

operation.summary: Creates an API-managed on-call schedule in the workspace.
operation.description: Creates an API-managed on-call schedule in the workspace. Provide a name and the complete list of shifts, then reference the returned schedule ID from a triage responsibility to use it for a team. An OAuth-created schedule is owned by that application for later updates and deletion. Duplicate IDs or external IDs are rejected.

operation.summary: Deletes an API-managed schedule and replaces linked triage responsibilities with available fallback users.
operation.description: Deletes an API-managed schedule and replaces linked triage responsibilities with available fallback users. The same ownership and team-management requirements as timeScheduleUpdate apply. Integration-synced schedules cannot be deleted here.

operation.summary: Requests a refresh of a schedule managed by an integration.
operation.description: Requests a refresh of a schedule managed by an integration. The schedule must have an associated integration. Success means the refresh was queued; the returned timeSchedule may still contain its previous shifts. Query the schedule again to read the refreshed entries.

operation.summary: Updates an unarchived, API-managed schedule.
operation.description: Updates an unarchived, API-managed schedule. Omitted fields remain unchanged; entries replaces every existing shift. OAuth callers can update only schedules created by the same application. Other callers need management permission for every team using the schedule, or workspace team management permission if no team uses it. Integration-synced schedules cannot be edited here.

operation.summary: Finds an unarchived schedule by its workspace-unique externalId and updates it, or creates one if none exists.
operation.description: Finds an unarchived schedule by its workspace-unique externalId and updates it, or creates one if none exists. For a new schedule, include name and the same externalId inside input; the lookup argument is not copied into input automatically. A supplied entries list replaces the old shifts. Email references without userId are matched to workspace users when possible; unmatched references remain external. The same ownership rules as timeScheduleUpdate apply to an existing schedule.

operation.summary: Submits an anonymous $pageview or $pageleave analytics event, with optional properties and session correlation.
operation.description: Submits an anonymous $pageview or $pageleave analytics event, with optional properties and session correlation. Unsupported event names return success=false. A successful response means tracking accepted the event, not that analytics delivery has completed. Limited to 30 requests per hour.

operation.summary: Creates the team’s triage responsibility using a manual user selection or an on-call schedule.
operation.description: Creates the team’s triage responsibility using a manual user selection or an on-call schedule. The team must be writable, the workspace plan must support triage responsibility, and the caller needs team management permission. A team can have only one rule. Selecting an integration-managed schedule also queues a refresh of its shifts.

operation.summary: Deletes a triage responsibility.
Updates the action or responsible users for a writable team’s existing rule.
operation.description: Updates the action or responsible users for a writable team’s existing rule. Changing to a manual selection clears its schedule, and changing to a schedule clears its manual selection. Omitted fields remain unchanged. Requires team management permission; selecting a different integration-managed schedule queues a refresh.

operation.summary: Changes the workspace role of a user.
operation.description: Changes the workspace role of a user. The requesting user must have a role equal to or higher than the target role. Requires workspace admin permissions.

operation.summary: Connects the Discord user to this Linear account via OAuth2.
Disconnects the external user from this Linear account.
Updates a specific user settings flag by performing an operation (e.g., increment or clear) on it.
Revokes all active sessions for a user, forcing them to re-authenticate.
operation.description: Revokes all active sessions for a user, forcing them to re-authenticate. Can only be called by a workspace admin or owner.

operation.summary: Revokes a specific authentication session for a user.
operation.description: Revokes a specific authentication session for a user. The admin cannot revoke their own sessions with this mutation. Can only be called by a workspace admin or owner.

operation.summary: Resets one or more of the user's setting flags.
operation.description: Resets one or more of the user's setting flags. If no specific flags are provided, all flags are reset.

operation.summary: Updates the settings record identified by id.
operation.description: Updates the settings record identified by id. You must own that record or have permission to manage workspace entities. General settings and notification category or channel preferences merge with existing values. See notificationDeliveryPreferences for its schedule replacement and mobile-channel effects.

operation.summary: Suspends a user, deactivating their account and revoking access to the workspace.
operation.description: Suspends a user, deactivating their account and revoking access to the workspace. The suspended user's sessions are invalidated. Can only be called by a workspace admin or owner.

operation.summary: Unlinks a guest user from their identity provider.
operation.description: Unlinks a guest user from their identity provider. Can only be called by an admin when SCIM is enabled.

operation.summary: Re-activates a suspended user, restoring their access to the workspace.
operation.description: Re-activates a suspended user, restoring their access to the workspace. Can only be called by a workspace admin or owner.

operation.summary: Updates a user’s profile.
operation.description: Updates a user’s profile. Use the user UUID or me for your own account. Updating another user requires member-management permission; identity-provider rules may block name changes, and application accounts only accept name and displayName.

operation.summary: Saves display settings for a view and scope.
operation.description: Saves display settings for a view and scope. Existing records that conflict with the supplied type, view type, and scope are deleted and replaced, so supply the settings you want to retain. Personal preferences are owned by the current user.

operation.summary: Deletes a saved preferences record, allowing the view to use its fallback defaults.
operation.description: Deletes a saved preferences record, allowing the view to use its fallback defaults. You can delete only your own user-type preferences. If the record is already absent, the mutation still succeeds.

operation.summary: Replaces the supplied settings objects on a saved preferences record.
operation.description: Replaces the supplied settings objects on a saved preferences record. You can update only your own user-type preferences; changing workspace defaults for a custom view also requires permission to edit that view.

operation.summary: Creates a webhook subscription and returns its configuration, including the signing secret.
operation.description: Creates a webhook subscription and returns its configuration, including the signing secret. Choose one team or all public teams, and provide a public HTTPS destination with the resource types you want to receive. The destination must not already be registered for the same team scope. Requires workspace API management permission; a team-specific webhook also requires that team’s management permission. AuditEntry subscriptions have separate audit log access requirements.

operation.summary: Deletes a webhook subscription and stops future deliveries.
Generates and returns a new HMAC-SHA256 signing secret for the webhook.
operation.description: Generates and returns a new HMAC-SHA256 signing secret for the webhook. Update your receiver to verify later deliveries with the returned key; the previous key is replaced rather than kept as a second active key. This changes webhook signatures, not the endpoint or subscribed event streams.

operation.summary: Updates an existing webhook without changing its team scope.
operation.description: Updates an existing webhook without changing its team scope. Omitted properties remain unchanged, and resourceTypes replaces the complete list of event streams. Setting enabled to false pauses delivery while retaining the subscription. Changing secret changes the key your receiver must use for later deliveries. Requires workspace API management permission and access to the subscribed resource types.

operation.summary: Archives an unused status so it is no longer available for new issues.
operation.description: Archives an unused status so it is no longer available for new issues. First move or archive every active issue in that status. You must be able to manage the team, and cannot archive reserved or inherited statuses or the last active status of a type.

operation.summary: Add an issue status to a team.
operation.description: Add an issue status to a team. Requires permission to manage the team; inherited workflows cannot be edited directly.

operation.summary: Update a status’s name, color, description, or position.
operation.description: Update a status’s name, color, description, or position. Requires permission to manage the team. Reserved and inherited statuses cannot be changed.
